Subject: MSA redlines - confidentiality carveout and uncapped damages for trade secrets

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — Atlas remains excited about Redwood’s latency profile for document redaction workloads. Our GC asked me to circulate the attached redline to the MSA. The key commercial/legal point is the confidentiality/trade-secret carveout: we need an explicit, uncapped damages exception for breaches involving Atlas trade secrets or other highly sensitive IP (we propose no cap and consequential damages available).

We realize this is a material ask so we included a short rationale in the attached markup and a proposed forensic-evidence and accelerated-remediation playbook (see Data_Protection_Schedule_Atlas.pdf). From our perspective this is a binary risk allocation item for the board. Can you confirm you received the redlines and who on your side will drive legal?

Requested next steps:
- Confirm receipt and point person for legal redlines
- Indicate whether Redwood will accept uncapped liability for trade-secret/confidentiality breaches or propose a narrowly scoped alternative
- If possible, provide an annotated counterproposal by EOD Friday 12/07

Appreciate it — Emma

Subject: RE: MSA redlines - confidentiality carveout and uncapped damages for trade secrets

Lauren/Marcus — I reviewed Atlas’s markup and Data Protection Schedule. High level reactions:

1) We cannot accept an unlimited, uncapped liability bucket for any class of incidents.
2) However, we recognize trade secrets/confidential information are material. Reasonable approaches to bridge: 
   - Narrow the carveout to: (i) willful and intentional disclosure (not accidental or negligent), and (ii) only for data types specifically enumerated in Schedule A (trade secrets, regulated PHI fields) with evidence standards.
   - Apply a higher, but defined cap (e.g., 3x annual contract value or $10M) for breaches meeting the narrow definition rather than unlimited exposure.
   - Add mandatory forensic investigation obligations and cost-shifting/remediation milestones with financial holdbacks tied to breach severity.

3) Consider offering a one-time supplementary insurance-backed arrangement (umbrella policy endorsement or escrowed remediation reserve) for enterprise customers with particularly sensitive data. That would make Atlas whole in practice while preserving predictability for Redwood.

4) Operational controls: tighten the Data Protection Schedule with minimums for encryption at rest/in transit, key management, access logs retention, and breach notification windows (48 hours initial notification). Atlas’s forensic playbook is reasonable; we can accept parts of it but need to preserve audit burden limits.

Marcus: from GTM/negotiation perspective, if Atlas insists on an uncapped clause we should push for either (a) a carveout limited to deliberate exfiltration with high evidentiary bar, or (b) an insurance/escrow solution. Either path needs commercial flexibility on $ and SOW.

I’ll draft a clean counterproposal and annotate the redline with the two compromise paths. ETA: EOD Thursday.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 06 Dec 2028 14:30:00 -05:00
Subject: Redwood counterproposal re: trade-secret/confidentiality carveout (redlines attached)

Emma — thanks for your patience. Attached is our annotated counterproposal. Key points: 

- We cannot accept an uncapped damages exception. Instead we propose a narrow, evidence-driven exception limited to: (i) proven willful exfiltration by Redwood personnel or a compromised Redwood private key that led to confirmed trade-secret disclosure; and (ii) material regulatory PHI exposures (as defined in Schedule A).
- For incidents that meet the narrow exception, we propose a special cap equal to the greater of (a) 3x annual contract value, or (b) $10,000,000.
- We will agree to consequential and special damages for those narrow exceptions (subject to the special cap).
- We’re willing to include additional operational commitments: 48-hour notification, expedited forensic report within 10 business days, quarterly security attestations for 12 months post-incident, and a remediation escrow equal to 3 months of average monthly fees (refundable if no qualifying incidents).
- Alternatively, if Atlas requires contractual unconditional uncapped liability, we request an insurance endorsement from Atlas’s side which names Redwood as a covered third party beneficiary for trade-secret incidents.

Please see attached file Atlas_MSA_redlines_20281204.docx for line-by-line edits and an Appendix with the proposed schedule language. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call tomorrow to go through the trade-secret definitions and forensic standards.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
attachments: (Redwood_MSA_counter_20281206.docx, redline_summary_20281206.pdf)

From: Emma Cole <emma.legal@atlashealth.com>

Date: Fri, 07 Dec 2028 16:42:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Redwood counterproposal re: trade-secret/confidentiality carveout (redlines attached)

Lauren/Rishi — appreciate the thoughtful counter. High-level response from Atlas GC and security: 

- We can live with a narrow definition but need the evidentiary standard to be: (i) independent forensic validation (third-party) and (ii) a presumption in favor of Atlas for exfiltration incidents unless Redwood can demonstrate full chain-of-custody and lack of intent.
- The proposed 3x ARR / $10M cap is closer to acceptable but the board wants a floor of $15M for companies handling clinical research trade secrets. They view potential downstream patient harm and competitive loss as catastrophic.
- Atlas is open to the remediation escrow concept and quarterly attestations; they prefer contractual language that entitles them to audit rights for 12 months after an incident.

They asked for a short call Monday 12/10 at 10am ET to finalize language (post-board). If you accept the $15M floor for clinical research datasets specifically (we can carve out other categories at lower caps), Atlas will present to the board with our compromise language.

Can we confirm Redwood’s position on: (1) $15M floor for clinical research trade secrets, and (2) acceptance of an independent third-party forensic presumption mechanism?

Thanks — Emma
Emma Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Atlas Health
